words.definition: （身体上或感情上）脆弱的，易受……伤害的；容易患……病的；易受……的攻击 / 袭击
words.etymology: c. 1600, from Late Latin vulnerabilis “wounding,” from Latin vulnerare “to wound, hurt, injure, maim,” from vulnus (genitive vulneris) “wound,”
examples:
Old people are particularly vulnerable members of our society.
老人是我们社会中特别容易受到伤害的成员。
words.mnemonic:
vulner（=to wound, injure：受伤；伤害）+ -able（形容词后缀，能
被……的）→能被伤害的→易受……伤害的，脆弱的；容易患……

words.mnemonic: velv-（=hair, down：（鸟的）绒羽，绒毛）+ -et（名词后缀）→在织

collocations: velvety skin：柔软的皮肤
words.definition: 光滑柔软的；柔和的；天鹅绒般的
examples:
The grass grew thick and velvety.
草长得又茂密又柔软光滑。
words.mnemonic: velvet（丝绒；天鹅绒）+ -y（形容词后缀）→天鹅绒般的→光滑柔

collocations: vultures circling / wheeling overhead：在头顶上空盘旋的兀鹫
words.definition: 秃鹫；乘人之危的人，趁火打劫的人
examples:
With no buyer in sight for the company as a whole, the vultures started to
circle.
因为眼下没有买家要买整个公司，趁火打劫的人开始打他们的主意。
words.mnemonic:
vult（=vul-=to pluck, tear：拔出；撕开）+ -ure（名词后缀）→把[猎
物，主要为大型动物的尸体]撕开者→秃鹫；趁火打劫的人

collocations: feel a revulsion against：对……感到厌恶

Most people viewed the bombings with revulsion.
大多数人对爆炸事件表现出惊恐不安。
words.definition: 极端厌恶；深恶痛绝；惊恐
examples:
She felt a deep sense of revulsion at the violence.
她对这一暴行深恶痛绝。
words.mnemonic:
re-（=away：离开）+ vuls-（=to pull：拉；拔；撕开）+ -ion（名词
后缀）→（猛烈、暴力地）拔出、撕开的行为→深恶痛绝；惊恐

examples:
The child went into convulsions.
那孩子全身抽搐起来。
words.mnemonic:
con-（强调前缀）+ vuls-（=to pluck, pull, tear：拔出；撕开）+ -ion
（名词后缀）→猛烈地（暴力地）撕开、拔出某物→痉挛，抽搐；
